title: An independent appointment investigation announced
summary: Cambridge announced an independent appointment investigation and said this case should not be generalised to staff of colour.
limit: An announcement is not a finding about allegations or the justification for the coverage.

title: A welfare review sets its scope
summary: Part One will examine the University’s support, decisions and communications, judged against what was known at each stage. The terms distinguish welfare questions from scrutiny of Arday’s academic record.
limit: These are terms of reference, not completed findings. Third-party media conduct and legal liability are outside this review’s remit; it cannot determine why he died.

title: CPS evidence to the inquest
summary: The witness statement records six prosecution reviews between 15 December 2019 and 13 February 2020 and three case-management panels. The CPS maintained that its charging decision was proper.
limit: Signed 28 July 2020; the website labels publication 10 November 2025. This is the prosecutor’s account, not a verdict on press conduct. Internal reviews do not prove editors knew about them during the coverage.

title: The inquest conclusion, reported by ITV
summary: ITV’s inquest report attributes to the coroner a conclusion of suicide and an account of distress about the impending criminal trial and publicity. It also records the family’s criticism and the police officer’s denial of bias.
limit: This is an inquest report, not the original Record of Inquest. Family accusations and witness evidence must be distinguished from the coroner’s conclusions. It does not allocate responsibility to individual outlets or establish a single cause.

title: Chelsea announces sanctions after the December match
summary: Chelsea said it permanently excluded one spectator for racially abusive language and threatening or aggressive behaviour, and temporarily excluded five others for abusive behaviour. It described its evidence process and appeal rights.
limit: A club ticketing decision under a civil standard, not a criminal conviction or a finding about press coverage. The statement does not say all six used racist language. The CPS did not bring criminal prosecutions.

title: A procedural ruling, before the merits decision
summary: The court struck three pleaded categories of allegation. Copyright was not in issue on this application.
limit: This did not decide whether the letter publication infringed privacy or copyright. The earlier bundle description of this ruling as substantive summary judgment has been corrected.

title: Privacy and copyright summary judgment
summary: The court granted summary judgment on misuse of private information and on copyright subsistence and infringement. A limited copyright co-authorship issue remained open.
limit: The decision concerns the challenged letter articles, not all reporting about Markle or a numerical threshold for acceptable coverage.

title: Publication of a copyright notice ordered
summary: The court set terms for print and online notices reporting its copyright finding. The May judgment records that publication was stayed pending an appeal application.
limit: An order is not proof the notice appeared on that date, and a court notice is not a voluntary apology. The remaining ownership issue and later appeal must retain their own dates.

title: Final copyright liability and account of profits
summary: The court resolved the remaining ownership issue in Markle’s favour, entered final summary judgment on copyright liability and gave directions for an account of profits.
limit: This did not quantify the profits or decide all privacy financial remedies. It confirms an article-specific legal result rather than a finding about the entire news cycle.

title: The appeal tests proportionate publication
summary: The appeal upheld the privacy outcome concerning five challenged articles. The court concluded that publication was not a proportionate response to the People article.
limit: This is a later legal finding about identified publications. It does not adjudicate every outlet’s coverage or disclose what editors knew at every earlier stage.

title: Ofcom’s consideration remained open at this date
summary: Ofcom’s FOI response said its consideration of the family’s concerns about ITV and Sky had not concluded.
limit: This is a dated procedural update, not an upheld breach. No later final merits decision was recovered in this research pass; that gap does not establish that none exists.

title: An independent review examines the disclosure
summary: The independent review concluded that releasing personal information on 15 February was avoidable and unnecessary, and examined police communications under intense news and social-media attention.
limit: The review assesses the police response; it is not a legal finding against each publisher or a complete count of online speculation. Personal health details are not repeated here.

title: Communication changes reported to the Accountability Board
summary: The Deputy Chief Constable reported that all but two actions from the review were complete. Media-engagement training and a peer review remained outstanding.
limit: These are recorded progress claims by the organisations involved, not an independent implementation audit or proof that wider media practices changed.

title: Three publications found to risk the course of justice
summary: The High Court found contempt concerning two Daily Mirror publications and one Sun publication. The Attorney General identified their dates and the risk to the course of justice.
limit: The finding applies to those specified publications, not all reporting. An arrest was a news development; it did not justify implying guilt.

title: Leveson examines the concentrated character attacks
summary: Leveson identifies the damaging three-day character coverage and records settlements by eight titles over 40 articles. Mirror editor Richard Wallace claimed off-record police briefings; Chief Constable Colin Port disputed this. The inquiry could not resolve that conflict.
limit: Sections 4.12–4.21 criticise appearance and temperament judgments and reckless publication, while finding no evidence of Mirror malice. The briefing dispute does not establish undisclosed incriminating facts. This is a later inquiry assessment, not a complete social-media census.

title: A later judgment records innocence and redress
summary: Paragraphs 7–11 record Jefferies’s innocence, admitted libel liability by eight newspapers over 40 articles, and a police settlement and apology in August 2013.
limit: This judgment’s legal issue was the government’s termination of Leveson Part Two. The background is primary judicial confirmation, not a new 2018 press-liability trial.
